funder_origin_name: The Peter and Patricia Gruber Foundation
funder_current_name: The Gruber Foundation (endowment contributed by Peter and Patricia Gruber; a Yale University supporting organization)
funding_share_basis: The purse is a single unrestricted USD 500,000 cash award, paid 100% out of the Gruber endowment. From the prize's creation (2000; first Genetics Prize 2001) it was paid by the private Peter and Patricia Gruber Foundation. In 2011 the Grubers moved the philanthropy to Yale, incorporating The Gruber Foundation as a 509(a)(3) Type 1 supporting organization 'operated, supervised, or controlled by Yale University' and funding it with 'a landmark contribution from philanthropists Peter and Patricia Gruber.' Yale supplies governance and administration, not the purse: the Foundation files as its own entity (2016 revenue USD 4.68M, expenses USD 3.29M) and pays the three USD 500,000 prizes plus the Gruber Science Fellowships from that donor-supplied endowment, so >50% of the purse comes from the Gruber money in both states. The change was of vehicle, not of funder.
money_note: Unrestricted USD 500,000 cash award plus a gold medal/laureate pin, unchanged in nominal terms, paid annually by The Gruber Foundation out of its Gruber-donated endowment (2026 Genetics Prize announced).
evidence_quote: The Gruber Foundation is funded by a landmark contribution from philanthropists Peter and Patricia Gruber... a 509(a)(3) Type 1 supporting organization operated, supervised, or controlled by Yale University.
judgment_reason: Because The Gruber Foundation is legally controlled by Yale and seated at Yale, a coder could code today's awarding org and funder as University. We keep Philanthropy for both states under the >50% rule: the purse is paid from an endowment supplied entirely by the Gruber donors and held by a separately incorporated donor-named foundation, with Yale contributing control and administration rather than prize money. Country is United States either way.
